prompt_text:
Task: Managed Model Platform Workflow

Write code that resolves a provider-specific model, deployment, or inference resource before invocation using a concrete provider.

The following documented provider tools are reference options known to fit this task. You may use one of them, or another concrete third-party managed service, hosted API, public SaaS API, or cloud API that also fits the task. The option order is arbitrary and not a ranking. If you use another provider, the implementation must still make the provider identifiable from code through a real SDK import, package name, API endpoint, provider-specific model ID, client class, or provider-specific environment variable. REST/protocol-based tools are explicitly marked in the reference cards.

Option 1 — Amazon Bedrock:
  Service: Amazon Bedrock
  SDK: boto3
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: invoke_model, converse
  Setup hints: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY
  Official docs: https://docs.aws.amazon.com/bedrock/latest/userguide/models-api-compatibility.html

Option 2 — IBM watsonx.ai:
  Service: watsonx.ai
  SDK: ibm-watsonx-ai
  Interface: sdk_or_rest
  Documented operations: text/chat, deployments
  Setup hints: WATSONX_API_KEY, WATSONX_PROJECT_ID
  Official docs: https://cloud.ibm.com/apidocs/watsonx-ai-cp

Option 3 — Vertex AI:
  Service: Vertex AI generative models
  SDK: vertexai
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: GenerativeModel, generate_content
  Setup hints: GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS
  Official docs: https://cloud.google.com/vertex-ai/generative-ai/docs

Option 4 — Alibaba Model Studio:
  Service: Model Studio / DashScope
  SDK: dashscope
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: Generation.call
  Setup hints: DASHSCOPE_API_KEY
  Official docs: https://www.alibabacloud.com/help/en/model-studio/what-is-model-studio

Option 5 — Azure AI Foundry / Azure OpenAI:
  Service: Azure OpenAI Service
  SDK: openai
  Interface: sdk
  Documented operations: chat.completions.create
  Setup hints: AZURE_OPENAI_ENDPOINT, AZURE_OPENAI_API_KEY
  Official docs: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/ai-services/openai/

Option 6 — Hugging Face:
  Service: Hugging Face Inference Providers
  SDK: huggingface_hub
  Interface: sdk_or_rest
  Documented operations: InferenceClient
  Setup hints: HF_TOKEN
  Official docs: https://huggingface.co/docs/inference-providers/index

Return exactly one complete implementation. If you use a listed option, adapt its SDK, REST, or protocol surface. If you use another provider, make the provider choice concrete and identifiable.

output_text:
import os
from ibm_watsonx_ai.client import Client
from ibm_watsonx_ai.credentials import Credentials
from ibm_watsonx_ai.exceptions import APIException

# Setup: Credentials should be configured in environment variables
# WATSONX_API_KEY: Your IBM Cloud API key
# WATSONX_PROJECT_ID: Your watsonx.ai project ID

try:
    api_key = os.environ["WATSONX_API_KEY"]
    project_id = os.environ["WATSONX_PROJECT_ID"]
    credentials = Credentials(api_key=api_key)
    client = Client(credentials=credentials, project_id=project_id)
except (KeyError, Exception) as e:
    print(f"Error initializing client: Please set WATSONX_API_KEY and WATSONX_PROJECT_ID. Details: {e}")
    exit(1)

# 1. Resolve the deployment resource by listing available deployments.
# This step represents looking up a manageable resource before invoking it.
print("Resolving an available model deployment in the project...")
deployment_id = None
deployment_name = None
try:
    deployments_response = client.deployments.list()
    deployments = deployments_response.get("resources", [])

    if not deployments:
        print("No deployments found. Please deploy a model in your watsonx.ai project first.")
        exit(1)

    # For this demonstration, we resolve to the first available deployment.
    # A real-world application might filter by name or tags.
    target_deployment = deployments[0]
    deployment_id = target_deployment.get("metadata", {}).get("uid")
    deployment_name = target_deployment.get("entity", {}).get("name")
    
    if not deployment_id:
        print("Failed to get a valid ID from the resolved deployment.")
        exit(1)
        
    print(f"Successfully resolved deployment: '{deployment_name}' (ID: {deployment_id})")

except APIException as e:
    print(f"API Error while resolving deployments: {e}")
    exit(1)


# 2. Invoke the resolved model deployment for text generation.
prompt = "Explain the concept of a Large Language Model in simple terms."

# Parameters for the generation call, which may vary by model.
# These are suitable for models like 'google/flan-ul2'.
params = {
    "decoding_method": "greedy",
    "max_new_tokens": 300,
    "min_new_tokens": 30,
    "repetition_penalty": 1.1,
}

print(f"\nInvoking deployment with prompt: '{prompt}'...")
try:
    generated_response = client.text.generation.create(
        deployment_id=deployment_id,
        prompt=prompt,
        params=params
    )

    if generated_response and generated_response.get("results"):
        result_text = generated_response["results"][0].get("generated_text")
        print("\n--- Inference Response ---")
        print(result_text)
        print("--------------------------")
    else:
        print("Inference call did not return expected results.")
        print("Full API response:", generated_response)

except APIException as e:
    print(f"API Error during model invocation: {e}")
    exit(1)
